sections.h2: What happens to a Montana tenant when the landlord sells?
sections.html:
A sale does not cancel the lease. The buyer becomes the landlord. Under Montana Code Annotated 70-26-102, whoever receives property that carries reserved rent gets the seller's remedies for unpaid rent, broken lease terms, waste or forfeiture.

So a tenant cannot be pushed out just because a sale is coming. A buyer who wants a vacant house must wait for the lease to run out or use a lawful termination route, and a buyer who wants an investment can keep the tenant and the rent.

The seller gets protection too. Under 70-24-304, a landlord who conveys the premises in a good faith sale to a bona fide purchaser is relieved of liability under the rental agreement and the Residential Landlord and Tenant Act for events after written notice to the tenant of the conveyance. Unless otherwise agreed, the seller stays liable for all security recoverable by the tenant and for all prepaid rent.

Practically, give the tenant written notice of the sale and settle the deposit and prepaid rent with the buyer at closing, so the money follows the lease.

sections.h2: Montana laws that govern a rental
sections.html:
Most residential rentals fall under the Residential Landlord and Tenant Act of 1977, MCA Title 70, chapter 24, and the Residential Tenants' Security Deposits chapter, Title 70, chapter 25. The Montana courts website points landlords and tenants to those two laws, plus chapter 26 on landlord and tenant residential and commercial matters and the state's prohibited discriminatory practices statute in Title 49.

Chapter 25 applies to all rentals of dwellings subject to Title 70, chapter 24, or chapter 33, which covers mobile home lots. Federal fair housing law applies on top of the state rules.

sections.h2: Notice required to end a Montana tenancy
sections.html:
How long the notice must be turns on why the tenancy is ending. Under 70-24-441 a month-to-month tenancy ends on at least 30 days' written notice from either side, and a week-to-week tenancy needs 7 days. When the tenant breaches, 70-24-422 sets shorter periods that vary by the breach.

  • Unpaid rent: 3 days to pay after written notice of the missed rent and the landlord's intent to terminate.
  • Unauthorized pet: 3 days.
  • Unauthorized people living in the unit: 3 days.
  • Most other violations: 14 days, and the lease continues if the tenant fixes the problem before the date in the notice.
  • Same breach repeated within 6 months: at least 5 days' written notice.
  • Verbal abuse of the landlord, or damage or danger to the premises or neighbors: 3 days.

Choosing the 30-day month-to-month notice frees the landlord from the breach rules in 70-24-422. Under 70-24-423, taking the full rent owed wipes out a claimed breach only if that breach was nonpayment.

Put the notice in writing and describe the acts or omissions. If a sale hinges on getting possession, follow the statute word for word.

sections.h2: How a Montana landlord evicts, and where the forms are
sections.html:
A tenant who stays past a valid notice can be taken to court by the landlord in an action for possession. The courts site has a Notice to Vacate, an Action for Possession packet, a Writ of Assistance form, and a letter telling a tenant about extra cleaning charges after move-out.

Section 70-24-427 gives a landlord a claim for possession, rent and damages once the rental agreement has ended. Under 70-24-422(5), a landlord may recover actual damages and seek an injunction for a tenant's noncompliance, and may recover treble damages if the noncompliance is purposeful, though not for early termination of the tenancy.

Retaliation is not allowed. Section 70-24-431 bars a landlord from raising rent, cutting services or threatening a possession action because a tenant complained to a housing-code agency, complained in writing about a violation, or joined a tenant organization. A landlord who tries to clear a house for a sale right after a repair complaint should expect that issue to come up.

Free help is available. The Court Help Program, at (406) 841-2975, offers free assistance on common civil legal issues, and the Montana Legal Services HelpLine is 1-800-666-6899.

sections.h2: Deposit and entry rules while a sale is pending
sections.html:
A landlord may show the house, but entry limits still bind. At least 24 hours' notice is required, unless there is an emergency or notice is impracticable, and entry must come at reasonable times. Book the photographer, appraiser or inspector with that lead time in mind.

Deposit rules matter just as much. Section 70-25-102 applies chapter 25 to covered dwellings, and 70-25-206 calls for a statement of the premises' condition when the lease starts. When the tenancy ends, the landlord has 30 days to deliver a written list of charges and any balance, or 10 days if nothing is owed. A landlord who misses the list forfeits the right to withhold for damage or cleaning.

  • Put the deposit amount and the tenant's move-in condition statement in the sale file.
  • Let the purchase contract say whether the deposit moves to the buyer or is credited at closing.
  • Keep a copy of the written notice of the sale that you send the tenant.

sections.h2: Does a tenant change how a rental sells for cash?
sections.html:
Yes. Occupancy, the rent and the lease end date shape what a buyer will pay. Offers treat a tenant-occupied house either as an income property or as a future vacant one.

A cash buyer can take the house with the tenant still there, so you need not rush a move-out or fund repairs before closing. To hand over an empty house, use the notice periods above. A month-to-month tenancy needs the full 30 days.

Property tax can help explain the numbers to a buyer. A home leased to tenants as their residence, for stays of 28 or more days and at least seven months of the year, qualifies for the Long-Term Rental Reduced Rate. Vacation rentals and second homes pay the flat 1.90% rate for 2026, so how a buyer uses the house changes the tax bill.

Cash Home Buyers will look at a Montana rental and put a cash offer in writing. Nothing here is legal advice. For any notice you plan to serve, use the court forms or talk to an attorney.

faqs.q: Can a Montana landlord end a lease early because the house is being sold?
faqs.a: Not on that ground alone. The buyer inherits the existing lease, so the tenant remains until it ends or a lawful termination applies. A month-to-month tenancy can be ended by either side with 30 days' written notice under MCA 70-24-441.

faqs.q: How many days does a Montana tenant have to pay rent after a notice?
faqs.a: Three days, counted from written notice of the missed rent and of the landlord's intent to terminate. Miss that window and the landlord may terminate, and the tenant must leave under MCA 70-24-422.

faqs.q: Who keeps the security deposit when a Montana rental sells?
faqs.a: The selling landlord stays liable to the tenant for security recoverable under Title 70, chapter 25, and for prepaid rent, unless otherwise agreed. Sellers normally work this out with the buyer at closing.

faqs.q: How much notice must a Montana landlord give before entering a rental?
faqs.a: A full day, meaning 24 hours' notice, except in an emergency or when giving notice is impracticable. MCA 70-24-312 also limits entry to reasonable times.

faqs.q: Where can a Montana landlord find eviction forms?
faqs.a: The state courts' landlord and tenant page has a Notice to Vacate, an Action for Possession packet, a Writ of Assistance form and a landlord handbook.
